shower.thought: You've never actually seen the color you're looking at—you've only seen your brain's interpretation of it, which might be completely different from what someone else sees.
The worst part about forgetting something isn't that it's gone—it's that you don't even know what you're missing.
You're statistically more likely to remember a lie you believed than a truth you were told once.
Time moves slower when you're not paying attention to it, which means boredom is actually your brain experiencing longer.
Every song you love is technically just organized noise that your brain decided means something.
You don't think in language until you try to explain your thoughts to someone else—before that, it's just pure feeling pretending to be an idea.
The reason you can't tickle yourself is the same reason you can't scare yourself—your brain always knows what you're about to do, so it can't be surprised by you.
You've probably met your soulmate already and had no idea, because you were having a bad day or they ordered the wrong coffee.
Most of your anxiety isn't about what's actually happening—it's about your brain's prediction of what might happen, which it treats as real.
Forgiveness might just be your brain choosing to stop rehearsing the same story about someone.
You only know you're dreaming after you've already started dreaming, which means you can never catch the moment consciousness switches modes.
Every photo you take is a moment you chose to stop experiencing.
You can't remember being born, so for the first few years of your life, you just... didn't exist, as far as your memory is concerned.
The older you get, the faster time passes, which means you experience less of your life the longer you live it.
You're the only version of you that will ever exist, but you have no idea if you're a good one or a bad one—only other people can judge that.
Your sense of humor is basically your brain's way of saying "I understand this contradiction and it delights me."
When you're lost in thought, your body is still operating on autopilot—you're technically two people at once, one awake and one asleep.
The last conversation you'll have with someone is always a regular conversation—you never know it's the last one.
You spend years learning to read, but no one teaches you how to stop—now you read everything, even things you don't want to.
Mirrors show you not how you look, but how you look in reverse—so the face you see is the one literally no one else ever sees.

darkjoke.thought:
My therapist asked what my biggest fear was.
I said, "That you're just as confused as I am but charging me $200 an hour to figure it out."

I told my dad he was a terrible father.
He said, "I know," and went back to ignoring me.

My friend said he's been sober for a year.
I said, "That's great!" He said, "No, it's terrible. I remember everything now."

I asked the funeral director why my uncle's casket was so expensive.
He said, "Quality craftsmanship." I said, "He's not going to notice."

My dating profile says I'm brutally honest.
Apparently that's code for "will make you cry before dessert arrives."

I told my mom I was seeing a therapist.
She said, "Finally," and I realized she'd been trying to get rid of me since 1987.

My accountant asked if I had any charitable donations.
I said, "Yeah—my existence has been a gift to everyone who avoided me."

I joined a gym and told the trainer I wanted to get in shape.
He looked at me and said, "I admire your optimism."

My partner said I never listen to her.
I wasn't really paying attention, but I'm pretty sure she seemed upset about it.

My doctor said I needed to cut back on drinking.
I found a new doctor.

I asked my boss for a raise.
He laughed so hard he had to catch his breath. I haven't seen him since.

My therapist said I have abandonment issues.
I told her she was right and asked if she could refer me to someone else.

I texted my ex "I miss you."
She replied, "You have the wrong number." Now I miss her even more.

My kid asked me if I was proud of him.
I said, "Ask me again when you're paying your own bills."

I told my best friend I was moving away.
He said, "Finally," and I realized we'd hated each other this whole time.

My barber asked how I wanted my hair cut.
I said, "In a way that makes people less likely to approach me." He said, "I'm already doing that."

I asked my wife what she wanted for her birthday.
She said, "Space." I started looking at apartments that day.

My psychiatrist asked about my childhood.
I said, "Where do I even start?" He said, "With a new psychiatrist, because this is going to take forever."

I told my dad I was disappointed in him.
He said, "Get in line," and I realized he was disappointed in himself too.

My relationship ended because my partner said I don't communicate.
I was going to explain, but what was the point?
